findings.title: The 'deterministic' check only reads propSlots' own cache, so it proves nothing
findings.claim: The per-ship test calls `expect(propSlots(stateOf(layout))).toEqual(slots)` straight after `propSlots(s)`. Both states share one propKey, so the second call returns the cached array itself. The determinism the spec lists as a unit test is never recomputed.
findings.evidence: plan L204 (test); plan L360-L367 and L391 (the one-entry module cache: `if (cached && cached.key === key) return cached.slots`); spec L71 ('propSlots (deterministic for a layout; ...)'); plan L1127 self-review claims it is covered.
findings.why: If propSlots ever picked up non-determinism (an unstable sort, a Set's iteration order), this test would still pass. Risk is low because the function is pure apart from the cache.
findings.fix: Clear the cache before recomputing: call `propSlots` on a state with a different key in between (for example the renamed-Skiff trick at L231, or another ship), then `expect(propSlots(stateOf(layout))).toEqual(slots)`. Or compare against `structuredClone(slots)` after evicting.

findings.title: Decision 5 says the starter slots are pinned in the test, but the test only counts them
findings.claim: Decision 5 says the listed slots, including the starter's (18,1) n, (4,8) n, (5,10) s and (1,10) s, are 'pinned in tests/propModel.test.ts'. The test pins exact slots only for the Cutter and Skiff; for the starter it checks only the counts (Crew Quarters 3, Medbay 1).
findings.evidence: plan L44 ('computed by propSlots, pinned in tests/propModel.test.ts') and L47 (the starter tiles); plan L198-L200 (only counts the starter); spec L71 requires only the Cutter and Skiff pinned.
findings.why: The spec is met, but a reader of Decision 5 or the gate text would think the starter's positions are under test when they are not.
findings.fix: Either pin the starter's four slots with `toEqual` like the Cutter's, or reword Decision 5 to 'Cutter and Skiff pinned; the starter's slots as computed (its counts are tested)'.

findings.title: The packs countColours test decodes every real pack twice under the default 5 s timeout
findings.claim: The new `it.runIf` test calls `countColours(cfg, read)` and `countColours(without, read)` with one `packReader`. `countColours` caches packs only within a call and `packReader` does not cache at all, so every pack (Maru, four LimeZu character sheets, three Pimen sheets) is decoded twice by pngjs. It is the first test to read the owner's real packs, and it runs under vitest's default 5 s timeout (vitest.config.ts:L10 sets none).
findings.evidence: plan L471-L476; scripts/art/buildPalette.ts:L37-L41 (per-call `packs` Map), L158-L163 (`packReader` reads with no cache); the existing buildPalette.test.ts:L26/L49 uses fixtures only; plan L91 and L928 already note load timeouts in the full suite.
findings.why: Under a loaded full run this could add another intermittent timeout on the owner's machine. Fresh clones skip the test.
findings.fix: Wrap the reader in a memo (`const cache = new Map(); const read = (p) => cache.get(p) ?? (cache.set(p, raw(p)), cache.get(p))`) so each pack is decoded once, and/or pass a timeout (`it.runIf(...)(name, fn, 30_000)`).

findings.title: The sector view rebuilds the propKey string every frame
findings.claim: `draw` calls `propKey(state)` every frame before it can return early. That builds a string from the layout hash and every room's `name/system` (17 rooms on the Cutter), about 60 times a second in the sector view and the duel.
findings.evidence: plan L719-L723 (propLayer.draw); plan L356-L358 (propKey); plan L786-L789 (called every frame after tiles.update).
findings.why: Small garbage-collection churn on a path that almost never changes; not a correctness issue.
findings.fix: Optionally check `state.layout` identity first (`if (state.layout === drawnLayout) return;`) and only compute propKey when the layout object changes, keeping propKey as the real cache key.
